## Weekly Budget Spending Snapshot

Your data shows a stable base from fixed costs, with the biggest movement coming from **Dining Out** and **Groceries**. The clearest visuals will be ones that separate steady categories from changing ones.

## Best Charts for Spending Patterns

| Chart Type | Best Use | Why It Works for This Data |
|---|---|---|
| **Stacked column chart** | Compare total weekly spend and category mix | Shows how each category contributes to each week’s total |
| **Line chart** | Track category trends over 4 weeks | Best for spotting rising or falling spending patterns |
| **Heatmap** | Find spikes by category and week | Quickly reveals which weeks are unusually high |
| **Grouped bar chart** | Compare categories week by week | Good for side-by-side category differences |
| **Area chart** | Show cumulative spending pressure | Useful for seeing how variable categories add up over time |

## Recommended Visualization Setup

### 1) Spending pattern overview
Use a **stacked column chart** with Week 1–Week 4 on the x-axis and spend on the y-axis.

- **Rent** and **Subscriptions** will appear flat, highlighting fixed costs
- **Groceries**, **Dining Out**, and **Entertainment** will show the most movement
- Total weekly spend becomes easy to compare at a glance

### 2) Trend detection
Use a **line chart** for the variable categories only:
- Groceries
- Dining Out
- Transport
- Entertainment

This makes upward drift, like Dining Out, much easier to spot than in a stacked chart.

### 3) Overspending focus
Use a **heatmap** or **conditional-format table** to highlight categories above their usual range.

## Overspending Category Chart Recommendation

**Best chart:** **Heatmap**

Why:
- It instantly shows which category-week cells are highest
- It makes overspending patterns obvious without extra interpretation
- It works especially well for categories with repeated increases, like **Dining Out** and **Entertainment**

## 3 Actionable Insights

- **Dining Out is the clearest overspending risk.** It rises every week from **120 to 180**, a **50% increase**, so this category should be reviewed first.
- **Groceries are trending upward.** They move from **180 to 240**, suggesting either inflation, more frequent shopping, or less meal planning.
- **Fixed costs are stable, so savings must come from variable spending.** Rent and Subscriptions stay flat, meaning the biggest control lever is discretionary spending like Dining Out and Entertainment.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Create Heatmap] https://www.google.com/search?q=budget+heatmap+spending+categories
Action: [Button: Compare Trend Charts] https://www.google.com/search?q=line+chart+vs+stacked+bar+chart+budget
